Class Semantics

java.lang.Object
pws.editor.semantics.Semantics
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public class Semantics extends Object implements Serializable
Represents a semantic domain as a normalized set of Configuration objects.

A Semantics is associated with a specific assembly (identified by assemblyId) and maintains a set of configurations that are automatically normalized: when adding a configuration, more specific (subsumed) configurations are removed to keep only the most general ones.

This class supports standard lattice operations:

  • OR(Semantics) - union of two semantics
  • AND(Semantics) - intersection of two semantics
  • NOT(Assembly) - complement relative to an assembly's universe
  • LEQ(Semantics, Assembly) - semantic implication check

    • addConfiguration

      public Semantics addConfiguration(Configuration config)
      Adds a Configuration to this Semantics with automatic normalization.

      The normalization ensures that:

      • If the new configuration is more specific (implies) an existing configuration, it will not be added (subsumed by existing).
      • If the new configuration is more general than existing configurations, those more specific configurations are removed.
      Parameters:
      config - the configuration to add
      Returns:
      this Semantics instance (for method chaining)
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the configuration belongs to a different assembly

    • OR

      public Semantics OR(Semantics other)
      Computes the union (OR) of this Semantics with another.

      The result contains configurations from both Semantics, with automatic normalization to remove redundant (more specific) configurations.

      Parameters:
      other - the other Semantics to union with
      Returns:
      a new Semantics representing the union
      Throws:

      public Semantics AND(Semantics other)

      Parameters:

      Returns:
      a new Semantics representing the intersection
      Throws:

      public Semantics NOT(Assembly assembly)

      Determines whether this Semantics implies another Semantics.

    • LEQ

      public boolean LEQ(Semantics other, Assembly assembly)
      Determines whether this Semantics logically implies another using universal evaluation.

      This method converts both Semantics to their SMProposition representations, evaluates each over all feasible assemblies, and then compares the results.

      Parameters:
      other - the Semantics to compare against
      assembly - the Assembly used to generate the universe of configurations
      Returns:
      true if this implies other for all feasible configurations; false otherwise
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the Semantics belong to different assemblies

    • simplify

      public Semantics simplify(Assembly assembly)
      Simplifies this Semantics by checking for each state in the assembly whether its single-state configuration implies this Semantics.

      For each state machine M and state S, if the configuration {M.S} implies this Semantics, that configuration is added (which may subsume others).

      Parameters:
      assembly - the Assembly instance to derive state machines and states from
      Returns:
      a new simplified Semantics
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if assembly ID doesn't match

    • transformByMachineEvent

      public Semantics transformByMachineEvent(String machineId, String eventName, Assembly assembly)
      Transforms this Semantics by applying an action A = M.E (machine M, event E).

      The transformation works as follows:

      1. Domain: Identify configurations containing {M:S} where S is a source state of transitions triggered by event E.
      2. Codomain: For each configuration in the domain, replace {M:S} with {M:T} where T is the target state of the triggered transition.
      3. Result: Return the codomain only. Configurations where the event cannot fire are discarded (strict event semantics).

      If multiple transitions are triggered by the same event, all are processed.

      Parameters:
      machineId - the identifier of the machine involved in the action
      eventName - the event triggering the transition
      assembly - the Assembly containing the machine definition
      Returns:
      a new Semantics with the transformation applied
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the machine or transition is not found

    • transformByMachineTransition

      public Semantics transformByMachineTransition(String machineId, Transition transition, Assembly assembly)
      Transforms this Semantics by applying a specific transition.

      Parameters:

      Returns:

    • computeCodomain

      public Semantics computeCodomain(String machineId, Assembly assembly, String sourceState, String targetState)
      Computes the codomain of a transformation by replacing state constraints.

      For each configuration in this Semantics that contains {machineId:sourceState}, creates a new configuration with {machineId:targetState} instead.

      Parameters:
      machineId - the machine identifier
      assembly - the Assembly (for creating result Semantics)
      sourceState - the source state name to replace
      targetState - the target state name to substitute
      Returns:
      a new Semantics with transformed configurations

      public Semantics complementHybrid(Assembly assembly)
      Computes the complement using a hybrid symbolic/enumeration approach.

      Converts this Semantics to SMProposition, negates it, and evaluates the negation over all feasible concrete assemblies.

      Throws:

    • computeReachableConfigurations

      public static Set<Configuration> computeReachableConfigurations(Configuration startConfig, Assembly assembly)
      Computes the set of configurations that are reachable from the given configuration via autonomous transitions in the assembly's component machines.

      A configuration C1 can reach configuration C2 if there exists an autonomous transition in some component machine M that changes M's state from S1 to S2, where C1 contains M.S1 and C2 is the result of replacing M.S1 with M.S2 in C1.

      Parameters:
      startConfig - the starting configuration
      assembly - the Assembly containing component machines with autonomous transitions
      Returns:
      set of configurations reachable from startConfig via autonomous transitions

    • findDeadlockConfigurations

      public Set<Configuration> findDeadlockConfigurations(Assembly assembly)
      Identifies "deadlock" configurations within this Semantics.

      A configuration is considered a deadlock if it cannot evolve internally via autonomous transitions of the component machines. This means no component machine in the configuration has an enabled autonomous transition from its current state.

      This is important for PWS semantics: a configuration that cannot evolve internally represents a potential deadlock unless it's covered by an outgoing transition in the controller.

      Parameters:
      assembly - the Assembly containing component machines with autonomous transitions
      Returns:
      set of configurations that are deadlocks (cannot evolve internally)

    • isFullyConnected

      public boolean isFullyConnected(Assembly assembly)
      Checks if this Semantics has full connectivity via autonomous transitions.

      Full connectivity means every configuration can reach every other configuration (possibly through intermediate configurations) via autonomous transitions.

      Parameters:
      assembly - the Assembly containing component machines
      Returns:
      true if all configurations are mutually reachable; false otherwise
